metadata.name: Product Management Agentic Skills Platform (PM ASP)
metadata.notes: This CALM model describes the runnable POC. Deferred components (MLflow, agentregistry publishing, RLS/multi-tenancy) are documented in ARCHITECTURE.md but omitted here as they are not yet built.

nodes.name: Author (TPM)
nodes.description: Product/eng user who asks the platform to create a PRD for a project.

nodes.name: Consumer (Stakeholder)
nodes.description: User who queries an existing project's requirements and gets a summary.

nodes.name: Chat UI
nodes.description: Next.js App Router chat surface. Renders markdown artifacts, shows the execution-plan chip and approval badge.

nodes.name: Backend (API Gateway + Intent Router + Skill Dispatcher)
nodes.description: FastAPI. Owns: request entry/CORS, the LLM intent router (Level-1 keyword fallback), skill dispatch, and persistence to the Conversation and Artifact stores.

router-contract.description: Every route returns the stable execution-plan contract {skill, context_sources, requires_approval, status, candidates}; status in matched|no_match|ambiguous.

nodes.name: agentgateway (LLM Gateway + MCP Router)
nodes.description: Single authenticated endpoint. Serves the Anthropic Messages API and routes MCP tool calls to the self-hosted MCP servers. Injects the upstream ANTHROPIC_API_KEY so callers never hold it.

llm-key-injection.description: The real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is held only in agentgateway's env and injected on the upstream request; the backend and n8n send a placeholder.

nodes.name: n8n (Workflow Engine)
nodes.description: Runs the skill workflows (generate_prd_v1, summarize_requirements_v1) triggered by webhook. Also owns approval state via wait nodes (M5, not yet built).

nodes.name: Postgres + pgvector
nodes.description: Skill Registry (seed), Conversation Store (conversations, messages), Artifact Store (artifacts). schema.sql. No executions table and no tenant_id by decision.

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.description: Session cache (session:{id}, 24h sliding). Other keys (streaming, approvals:pending, rate limiting, router cache) are documented seams. See redis-key-patterns.md.

nodes.name: Anthropic (Claude)
nodes.description: External LLM provider reached only through agentgateway.

nodes.name: Atlassian MCP (Jira + Confluence, self-hosted)
nodes.description: Self-hosted MCP server, Data Center, PAT auth. Jira + Confluence share one credential boundary → one server. Runs on the user's host, reached via host.docker.internal. Context-fetch wiring is an M4 seam.

credential-boundary.description: One MCP server per credential/trust boundary. The Atlassian PAT lives with this server; the app never holds it.

nodes.name: GitHub MCP (self-hosted)
nodes.description: Self-hosted GitHub MCP server, PAT auth — its own credential boundary, its own agentgateway target. Runs on the user's host. Context-fetch wiring is an M4 seam.

credential-boundary.description: Separate credential boundary from Atlassian; the GitHub PAT lives with this server.

nodes.name: Docker Compose network
nodes.description: Single-tenant local dev boundary. Internal services trust each other; agentgateway has no client-side auth here (RBAC deferred to M9). Production target is Kubernetes/Helm.

relationships.description: Author chats to create a PRD.
Intent router asks Claude to pick a skill (real mode). Falls back to Level-1 keyword routing offline / on error.
Backend triggers the matched skill's n8n workflow by webhook (workflow_ref from the registry).
Persist conversations/messages/artifacts; read latest artifact by project for the summarize skill.
Workflow calls Claude to author the PRD / write the summary.
SEAM (M4, not yet wired): the generate_prd workflow will fetch project context via MCP before calling the LLM.
agentgateway forwards to Anthropic, injecting the API key.
MCP tool routing to the self-hosted Atlassian server (host.docker.internal).
MCP tool routing to the self-hosted GitHub server (host.docker.internal).
The six services run in Docker Compose for local dev (Kubernetes/Helm in production).

flows.name: Journey 1 — Author generates a PRD
flows.description: Chat message → LLM intent router picks generate_prd → n8n workflow authors the PRD via Claude (+MCP context, M4) → artifact stored in Postgres → returned to the UI (pending approval).

transitions.description: POST /api/chat; backend persists the user message
LLM router returns {skill: generate_prd, requires_approval: true}
Trigger generate_prd_v1 webhook with the project + requirements
SEAM (M4): fetch Jira/Confluence/GitHub context via MCP

flows.name: Journey 2 — Consumer queries requirements
flows.description: Chat message → LLM router picks summarize_requirements → backend fetches the latest stored PRD → n8n summarizes it via Claude → summary returned to the UI.

transitions.description: "what are the requirements for project Atlas"
POST /api/chat; backend persists the user message
Read latest generate_prd artifact for the project
Trigger summarize_requirements_v1 with the stored PRD content

human-approval.description: generate_prd is requires_approval=true. Surfaced as a UI badge in the POC; enforcement (n8n wait node) is deferred to M5. Approval state lives in n8n, never in Postgres.

multi-tenancy.description: Single-tenant only through Phases 1–2. No tenant_id / RLS yet; revisited at M9 (edge-only vs. threaded-through-every-store + Postgres RLS + per-tenant MCP credential scoping).
